title: GrantThai MCP tools (implemented in v0.1, extended for the v0.3 router; grantthai.mcp)
description: Version 0.4.0-draft. The MCP tool surface, a one-to-one wrapper over the same library functions the CLI uses (grantthai.api_py). Implemented in src/grantthai/mcp (docs/mcp.md); the `examples` entry below is the implemented tool list and tests/mcp checks the server against it. Hard rules: (1) no MCP tool may set any field's status above DRAFT (spec/common/status_permissions.yaml, hard_ceiling); (2) no MCP tool can submit anything to NRIIS or any fund; (3) validation over MCP is REPORT-ONLY (status_effect: none); (4) every value written over MCP is recorded as AI-assisted and can never be provenance_class SOURCE. (5) every value written over MCP records the AI tool (name, version, stage) in authoring.ai_use_declaration.tools; it never sets declaration_confirmed_by_human, which only the researcher sets (docs/policy/ai-use-ceiling.md). The CLI and MCP share the same checking code, so the findings are identical. (6) v0.3 router: the output route is the researcher's choice. grantthai_build and grantthai_validate take an optional `route`; with none, the server resolves it only from what a person declared (routing.default_route, a legacy project.yaml, the one default route of the work_type). When that does not decide, the tool returns the candidate list and builds nothing; the server MUST NOT default the route. grantthai_list_routes lists, grantthai_check_route reports for an explicit route, grantthai_new_project takes an optional work_type (writes work.yaml 0.3). Every tool stays capped at DRAFT.

wraps_cli_command.description: Must name an existing human CLI command (spec/common/parity.yaml requires a tested human equivalent).

status_effect.description: none = report-only, persists nothing; draft_only = may write field values at status DRAFT or below.
